name: Slagside Rivet-Crown Scrap Helm
description: Assembled from salvaged pressed-steel panels, corrugated conduit strips, and cracked polycarbonate face shields bolted together with mismatched rivets. The surface is mottled rust-orange, soot-black, and bare aluminum where paint has been ground away. Padding inside is layered transit foam and cut bicycle tire. Horn cutouts are crudely torched open and filed smooth. Fit varies — most are adjusted with wire wrapping at the crown.
functionality: Partial acid-rain deflection, blunt impact resistance, and face-shield coverage. Horn cutouts accommodate most common geneware. No electronics. Some builds include a crude wire-mesh filter over the mouth opening.
what_it_says: You built your own armor because no one was going to give it to you.
manufacturer: Slagside (self-made, the Gray Zone fabrication collective)
story_hooks: A recurring rivet stamp — a small triangle — appears on helmets across three different the Gray Zone districts, suggesting a single traveling builder or a copied template with significance no one will explain.
A Tier 3 urban anthropologist is collecting these helmets for a gallery show; the Gray Zone residents are now deliberately making them uglier to sabotage the exhibit.
One helmet has a sealed compartment welded into the crown. It's been passed between owners for eleven years. Nobody has opened it.

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutalist industrial helmet with a jagged, asymmetrical crown silhouette. Appears jury-rigged from scrap metal panels welded and bolted together. Evokes a Mad Max aesthetic merged with working-class tool-wear. Sits heavy and deliberate on the head, suggesting both protection and intimidation.
physical_description.fit: Loose to semi-fitted depending on wire-wrap adjustment at crown. Interior padding creates variable comfort. Horn cutouts sit high above natural hairline. Designed for function over ergonomics — wearer adjusts fit to personal need.
physical_description.primary_material: Salvaged pressed-steel panels, corrugated steel conduit strips, cracked polycarbonate face shields, transit foam padding, recycled bicycle tire rubber lining
physical_description.texture: Surface is rough and scarred — oxidized rust patches, ground-smooth bare aluminum, soot residue, filed edges. Bolts protrude slightly. Interior padding is soft but uneven. Face shield is clouded and scratched.
physical_description.color_scheme: Mottled rust-orange dominating, deep soot-black accents, exposed brushed aluminum, hints of faded paint. No cohesive palette — pure salvage aesthetics.
physical_description.closures: Mismatched bolts and rivets throughout. Wire wrapping around crown for sizing adjustment. No traditional fastening — sits via weight and pad pressure.
distinctive_features: Crude torch-cut horn cutouts, filed smooth
Visibly bolted polycarbonate face shield panels
Exposed corrugated conduit strips forming structural ribs
Heavy patina and rust oxidation across all surfaces
Asymmetrical assembly with no two bolts matching
Bare metal patches where coating has worn through
Interior bicycle tire rubber lining for shock absorption
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 5 sub-grade salvage. Raw material cost near zero. Signals ungoverned fabrication and resource scarcity.
physical_description.cultural_context: Slagside the Gray Zone collective — autonomous maker community operating outside corpo supply chains. Wearer is either a scrap worker, Behemoth salvager, or militant sub-grade operative. Anti-establishment signal.
physical_description.condition_typical: Always weathered and patched. Fresh welds and new bolt additions common. Never pristine. Visible repair history is the design.
